2608.24632.title: Causal Modelling of Support Interventions for Student Competency Assessment
2608.24632.paper_summary: Accurate assessment of student competencies is essential for enabling educators to identify individual needs, design targeted interventions, and evaluate the effectiveness of educational strategies. Empirical assessment procedures are typically grounded in psychometric models, such as item response theory, which relate student competence levels to performance on assessment tasks. In this paper, we advocate adopting a structural causal modelling approach to educational assessment, moving beyond probabilistic belief updating toward a framework that explicitly supports interventional and counterfactual reasoning. We propose a corresponding protocol for its construction and analyse the practical relevance of forms of reasoning that remain inaccessible to standard associative models, including the explicit modelling of interventions such as hints and the related counterfactual scenario analysis. Although our protocol requires the structural equations to be elicited from experts, the necessary information is purely logical and does not rely on probabilistic, less tenable assumptions. We illustrate the approach using data from an assessment that employs complex tasks designed to measure compulsory school student algorithmic skills.
2608.24632.paper_summary_zh: 準確評估學生能力對於使教育者能夠識別個別需求、設計針對性的干預措施以及評估教育策略的有效性至關重要。實證評估程序通常基於心理測量模型，例如項目反應理論，這些模型將學生的能力水平與評估任務的表現相關聯。在本文中，我們主張採用結構性因果模型方法進行教育評估，超越概率信念更新，朝向一個明確支持干預和反事實推理的框架。我們提出了一個相應的建構協議，並分析了那些對標準聯想模型仍然無法接觸的推理形式的實際相關性，包括對提示等干預措施的明確建模以及相關的反事實情境分析。儘管我們的協議要求從專家那裡引出結構方程，但所需的信息純粹是邏輯性的，並不依賴於概率性和不太可靠的假設。我們使用來自一項評估的數據來說明這種方法，該評估使用設計用於測量義務教育學生算法技能的複雜任務。
